physical: An induced current flows so as to oppose the change that produced it; a coil opposes a change in its own current with a back-EMF proportional to its inductance. (EMF = L × dI ÷ dt)
reflected_sentence: An induced flow moves to receive the change that produced it, so changing a flow across Expansion gets easier as receptivity and alignment rise.
rule_reason: One cost caused by resistance ('changing the current' rises with 'inductance', which carries resistance) turns the relationship around so what got harder with opposition gets easier with receptivity.
interpretation: Because inductance is opposition to a change in flow, its single resistance cost turns the reading around. What opposed change on the physical side becomes receptive to change across Expansion on the nonphysical side.
closing: The rule decisively turns this relation around because it has an odd number (1) of costs caused by a quantity that carries resistance (inductance). Back-EMF, inductance, and electric current have no partners in the frozen vocabulary and are recorded in unmapped_terms.
